suite: packages/skotiq_app: test/screens/dashboard + test/screens/onboarding + test/screens/shell + test/localization + observing_site_gating + flat_failure_banner + contextual_tour_prompt = 382 pass, 6 fail. All 6 failures are captures_landscape_test golden-image cases (4 dashboard, 2 onboarding). Those goldens are gitignored local artifacts (.gitignore:298 `**/test/**/captures/`) captured 2026-07-20 and 2026-06-05 respectively — before ~250 UI fixes landed in this campaign — and fail at 27-42% pixel diff, including on panes I never touched (the Settings root list, the onboarding Welcome step). Pre-existing environment drift, not a regression. `dart analyze lib` clean in packages/skotiq_app and apps/desktop; `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` clean on every file I touched (the 7 files it still flags are other agents' concurrent edits).

fixes.title: 'Use Device Location' is IP geolocation labelled as GPS, and it leaves the old elevation in place
fixes.summary: The Settings half was genuinely closed by an earlier wave (location_settings.dart:256-269 titles the row 'Detect Location' with an honest subtitle; :520-527 asks first; :576-585 clears an inherited elevation past 25 km). But the SAME service has a second production caller the finding never reached, and it was worse: the first-run wizard. OnboardingSiteStep._seedFrom posted a frame callback that called GeolocationService.fetchLocation the instant the step appeared, with no site on record — the app's first outbound request, on its first run, sending the machine's public IP to ipapi.co (falling back to plain-HTTP ip-api.com), with no click and nothing on screen saying so. Its 'Use my current location' button called fetchLocationFromGPS() with no consent, reported failure as 'Could not get GPS location. Check permissions.' (the same GPS mislabel) and wrote lat/lon while leaving the stored elevation attached to the new position. Fixed at the cause: the automatic lookup is gone (site_step.dart:141-147 sets _offerIpEstimate and nothing else); the suggestion card now states what would be sent BEFORE anything is sent and carries an 'Estimate from IP' button; both affordances route through one shared confirmGeolocationLookup() (new lib/widgets/geolocation_consent.dart) that Settings now uses too, so the two surfaces cannot describe the request differently or one of them forget to ask; and _useDeviceLocation applies the same 25 km rule (site_step.dart:319-336), clearing the elevation and the field and saying so.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/onboarding/onboarding_steps_test.dart -> 'no lookup leaves the machine until the user asks' (counts calls through onboardingApproximateLocationProvider: 0 on arrival, 0 after pressing the button, 0 after declining, 1 only after accepting; also asserts the pre-request disclosure and that the dialog names ipapi.co) and 'detecting a location asks first and drops a stale elevation' (seeds Seattle 47.6062/-122.3321/1234 m, drives a Newtown Square PA fix, asserts the lookup did not run before consent and that observer_elevation lands at 0). The two pre-existing suggestion-card tests were updated to go through the explicit request — they encoded the auto-fire.
fixes.revert_check: (1) Re-added the post-frame `unawaited(_lookUpIpEstimate())` in _seedFrom -> 'no lookup leaves the machine until the user asks' FAILED (expected 0 calls, got 1: 'the step looked up a location on its own'). (2) Replaced `elevation: keepElevation ? null : 0,` with `elevation: null,` in site_step.dart:329 -> 'detecting a location asks first and drops a stale elevation' FAILED (expected 0.0, actual 1234.0). Restored both -> 18/18 onboarding + 29/29 with location_settings_truth_test pass.
fixes.caveats: GeolocationService itself is unchanged: the ip-api.com fallback is still plain HTTP. It is now only reachable behind a dialog that names it, which is the disclosure the finding asked for, but an https-only fallback would be better.

fixes.title: Timezone picker is inert: all 18 options are IANA names, and the clock parser accepts none of them
fixes.summary: Most of this was closed before I got here and I verified it rather than taking it on trust: the picker now offers only offsets the parser honours (location_settings.dart:452 feeds kUtcOffsetTimezones at :867; a stored IANA label is migrated through kLegacyIanaUtcOffsets at :843-855), and the surfaces the verifier said were the REAL cause now read clockProvider — status bar at status_bar/temperature_and_time.dart:161, dashboard header at dashboard_header_actions.dart:102, night timeline at night_timeline.dart:41, moon card at moon_card.dart:37. What was NOT closed is one more clock FACE on the same screen: the Dashboard command bar's night-context chip renders 'Sunset HH:MM' and formatted the raw DateTime (command_bar.dart's `_formatClock(DateTime)`), so a site on UTC+09:00 showed the laptop's sunset time directly beside a header clock showing the site's. Two zones on one screen with nothing saying which is which is worse than uniformly host-local. `_formatClock` now takes a Clock and `resolveNightContext` takes it as a REQUIRED named parameter (command_bar.dart:186-191, :200-208) — required rather than defaulted, because a silent `const SystemClock()` default is exactly how this survived four waves — and NightContextChip supplies `ref.watch(clockProvider)`.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/dashboard/night_context_chip_timezone_test.dart -> 'the sunset face follows the chosen site timezone' (pumps the production NightContextChip through the real provider graph with app_settings timezone=UTC+09:00 and useSystemTime=false; sunset is pinned at 20:14 UTC, asserts 05:14 renders and 20:14 does not) and 'a site on UTC reads the UTC face'. Plus a pure-resolver case in command_bar_test.dart -> 'the sunset face follows the chosen site timezone'.
fixes.revert_check: Replaced `resolveNightContext(twilight, now, clock: clock)` with `clock: const SystemClock()` at the production call site in NightContextChip.build — the WIRING, not the resolver. Both widget cases FAILED. Restored -> 2/2 widget + 12/12 command_bar_test + 25/25 with observing_site_gating_test pass.
fixes.caveats: FixedOffsetClock is a fixed offset with no DST rule, and timestamps outside the dashboard/shell (FITS headers, log lines) stay host-local — both are pre-existing and stated in the Timezone row's own subtitle.

fixes.title: Selecting Spanish translates only the nav rail and Settings; every other screen stays English
fixes.summary: Wave 5 left this 'partial': it localised the status bar and made the picker's label honest, then stopped, because the rest is 'a translation program'. That reasoning is right about Imaging/Sequencer/Analytics and wrong about the one screen the finding actually evidenced — the Dashboard is the LANDING screen, and a language picker whose first result is a 100% English home screen reads as broken rather than partial. So the briefing is now wired to the catalogue: cockpit_standby.dart (TONIGHT'S BRIEFING, No run active, Image tonight, Plan Tonight + its tooltip), standby/tonight_targets_card.dart (Tonight's targets, the planning/error/retry states, Set location, Open planner, Exposure/Usable/Score), standby/moon_card.dart (Moon, all eight phase names, '{value}% illuminated', Moonrise, Moonset), standby/readiness_card.dart (Readiness, the four device chips, Connect equipment, Checking disk…, Disk query failed, Set a capture directory…, Free storage), standby/last_night_recap_card.dart (Last night/Last run, No runs yet…, the stat chips, the four run-status labels and the whole relative-time ladder), standby/night_timeline.dart (the no-location sentinel, the four axis tick labels, and the countdown header) and dashboard_header_actions.dart (Edit Dashboard/Edit/Done/Widgets/Reset, the edit-mode hint, and the three LST tooltips, which now reuse the statusLst* keys the status bar already had). 84 keys in both locales. Two structural changes rather than string swaps: NightCountdown.headlineLabel became headlineLabelKey (night_timeline.dart:191-195) because a pure resolver returning finished English is how that header stayed English, and _TimelinePainter now takes a SkotiqLocalizations (:328-334) since a CustomPainter has no BuildContext. The briefing's date line also stopped hard-coding English month/day tables AND DateTime.now(): it is MaterialLocalizations.formatMediumDate over clockProvider.now(), so it is both translated and on the site's timezone. The setting's own scope claim was updated in both locales to name the Dashboard and to keep naming what stays English.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/dashboard/standby_localization_test.dart -> 'the night briefing follows the chosen language' (pumps the real CockpitStandby under Locale('es') and asserts RESUMEN DE ESTA NOCHE / Ninguna sesión activa / Capturar esta noche / Objetivos de esta noche / Preparación / Conectar el equipo / Última sesión / 'Todavía no hay sesiones…' render AND that every English literal the audit read off the Spanish build does not), 'the moon card translates the phase and the readout' (74% Waning Gibbous -> 'Gibosa menguante' + '74 % iluminada'), and 'an English build is untouched'.
fixes.revert_check: (1) Put `'No run active'` back in place of `l10n.text('dbNoRunActive')` in cockpit_standby.dart -> 'the night briefing follows the chosen language' FAILED; the English case still passed. (2) Put `moon.phaseName` back in place of `context.l10n.text('dbMoonPhase${moon.phaseName}')` -> 'the moon card translates the phase and the readout' FAILED. Restored both -> 3/3 pass.
fixes.caveats: Scope is now chrome + Dashboard. Imaging, the Sequencer, the planner and Analytics remain English and the picker still says so and still marks Spanish '(beta)' — that residue is a translation program, not a wiring bug. An unrecognised run status is echoed verbatim rather than translated (it is data, not copy).

fixes.title: Importing a detailed .hor horizon silently collapses it to 8 sector maxima
fixes.summary: Closed, and I re-read the code rather than trusting the prior claim. location_settings.dart:672-712 _confirmHorizonReduction runs BEFORE anything is stored: it states the sample count, that Skotiq keeps eight 45° sectors with only the tallest sample per sector applied across the whole sector, 'At most 8 of the 36 survive' (:684, an upper bound rather than an exact discarded count, because samples can pile up in one sector), and the consequence in the operator's own terms — 'part of a sector that is really clear will be treated as blocked and the planner will skip targets there' (:700-702). It then lists the eight values it is about to store, and Cancel leaves the existing mask untouched. This matches the verifier's own reading that the shippable defect is the silence, not the number: the 8-sector model is the app's horizon model everywhere (horizonDirections) and max-per-sector is the conservative direction.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/location_horizon_import_disclosure_test.dart -> 'the import states the sample count and what it drops', 'shows the eight values it is about to store', 'cancelling leaves the existing mask untouched', 'accepting stores the sectors and the message reports the reduction', 'a single-sample file is not reported as dropping samples'. Re-run green this wave.
fixes.revert_check: Not re-reverted this wave (no code change of mine). Wave 5 recorded: deleting the reduction sentence made 'the import states the sample count and what it drops' fail with 'Found 0 widgets with text containing At most 8 of the 36'.
fixes.caveats: The stored model is still eight sectors. A full interpolated profile is a feature, not a defect fix.

fixes.title: Settings search is a raw substring match, so 'capture folder' returns 'No settings match your search'
fixes.summary: Closed at the matcher the verifier's correction named, and I re-derived the finding's three repros against the current code rather than re-running someone else's test. settings_screen.dart:178 splits the query and requires EVERY token to match — `tokens.every((token) => sectionMatchesToken(section, token))`; sectionMatchesToken (:44-50) falls through to kSettingsSearchSynonyms (:30-40), which carries the app's own vocabulary for files-storage: 'capture folder', 'capture directory', 'save path', 'image folder', 'disk space', 'free space', 'storage location'. So 'capture folder' matches as a phrase; 'disk' matches as a substring of 'disk space'; 'free space' matches token-by-token; 'save path' likewise. SettingsSectionDef.matches survives as the per-token predicate, which is correct — tokenisation belongs to the caller.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/settings_search_query_test.dart -> 'a two-word phrase finds the page that owns the setting', 'every token still has to match something', 'an autofocus term does not land on Files & Storage', 'the best match is listed first'. Re-run green this wave.
fixes.revert_check: Not re-reverted this wave. Wave 5 recorded: restoring `if (section.matches(query))` made the screen render 'No settings match your search.' for 'capture folder' — the finding's exact repro.

fixes.title: Files & Storage says 'Last backup: Never' while Backup & Restore says a real timestamp
fixes.summary: Closed twice over, and this is the P1 so I traced both paths myself instead of accepting the claim. (1) auto_save_settings.dart:169 watches autoSaveLifecycleProvider, not the raw autoSaveServiceProvider; the lifecycle provider (auto_save_service.dart:785-810) is the only thing that loads the persisted autosave.* keys and calls start(config, lastBackup), and start() both stores the hydrated timestamp and PUBLISHES it (:154-166) so a listener that attached pre-hydration is not left on the stale status — the exact hole that produced 'Never'. Because the lifecycle provider `ref.watch`es the service provider, a backend swap rebuilds BOTH, so the fresh instance is re-hydrated rather than left un-started (start()'s `if (_started) return;` can no longer strand it). (2) Independently, auto_save_settings.dart:193 reads `ref.watch(autoSaveStatusProvider).valueOrNull ?? service.status`, and autoSaveStatusProvider (auto_save_service.dart:762-778) backfills lastBackup from BackupService.lastBackupSettingKey — the same key Settings > Advanced > Backup & Restore reads via backup_screen.dart:432. Both paths read PERSISTED state, which is why the finding's stronger repro (stop, relaunch, reopen the page) is covered.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/auto_save_settings_hydration_test.dart -> 'Status shows the persisted last backup, not "Never"' (seeds autosave.last_backup_at 2 h old into the DB, pumps the production AutoSaveSettings, asserts '2h ago' renders and neither 'Never' nor 'Pending' does), plus the schedule-hydration and no-clobber cases. Re-run green this wave.
fixes.revert_check: Not re-reverted this wave. Wave 5 recorded the important subtlety: reverting EITHER path alone leaves the test passing, because the other still renders the truth; reverting BOTH fails it with 'Found 0 widgets with text "2h ago"'. Worth keeping on the record — a single-line revert does not sever this claim.

fixes.title: Automatic backups are ON by default and write to a location the Files & Storage page never names and offers no way to change
fixes.summary: Both reproduced halves are closed. PATH: backup_service.dart:1051-1055 _getBackupDirectory calls resolveDefaultBackupDirectory (:130-139), which joins 'backups' onto the parent of the RESOLVED database file and therefore honours SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR — the verifier confirmed this live (a sandboxed instance wrote into its own data dir; ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups received nothing). DISCLOSURE: file_path_settings.dart:267-310 renders a 'Backups' row whose subtitle is the resolved path (asked of backupServiceProvider.getBackupDirectory() through backupDirectoryPathProvider at :53, so it cannot drift from what the service actually uses) followed by an UNCONDITIONAL retention sentence — 'Automatic backups are written here, beside the database; "Maximum backups" deletes the oldest bundles from this folder' — which renders even while the path is still resolving or has failed. It carries an Open-folder / Copy-path action. Settings > Files & Storage is FilesAndStorageSettings, which renders FilePathSettings and AutoSaveSettings on ONE page, so that row is on the same scroll as the retention control it describes.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/file_path_backup_folder_test.dart -> 'the backup folder is named on the page', 'the row says retention deletes from that folder', 'the folder can be opened from the row', 'an unresolvable folder still states the retention policy'. Re-run green this wave.
fixes.revert_check: Not re-reverted this wave. Wave 5 recorded: renaming the row title to 'Backups (severed)' made 'the backup folder is named on the page' fail.
fixes.caveats: A user-SELECTABLE backup folder is still not built — that needs a new persisted setting plus BackupService write/list/restore plumbing, and neither reproduced defect (undisclosed path, ignoring the configured data dir) survives without it.

fixes.title: The Alpaca server address can never be set
fixes.summary: Closed, and I checked the half that would make this a RELOCATED fix rather than a real one — whether anything actually READS the setting. connection_settings.dart:201-217 renders an 'Alpaca Server Address' row whose subtitle is the live `${settings.alpacaServerHost}:${settings.alpacaServerPort}` and whose Configure button opens AlpacaServerDialog (connection_settings_alpaca_dialog.dart:64-66), which writes through setAlpacaServerHost / setAlpacaServerPort — the skotiq_core setters that had zero UI callers. It sits directly above the 'Query Alpaca on startup' toggle (:218-227) so 'the configured Alpaca server' now has a referent. Crucially the value is consumed: unified_discovery_provider.dart:394-401 resolves the Alpaca discovery target as `host ?? settings.alpacaServerHost` / `port ?? settings.alpacaServerPort` and hands it to deviceService.discoverAlpacaAtAddress, and the startup path reaches it through auto_discovery_launcher.dart:109 (`includeAlpaca: settings.alpacaAutoDiscover`) -> discoverAll -> discoveryBackendsForPolicy. So the address is written by the new row and read by the discovery it claims to configure.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/connection_alpaca_address_test.dart -> 'the Alpaca address is shown and can be changed' (asserts the stored alpacaServerHost becomes 192.168.1.47 and alpacaServerPort 32323 and that the subtitle re-renders them), 'a malformed port is refused rather than coerced'. Re-run green this wave.
fixes.revert_check: Not re-reverted this wave. Wave 5 recorded: corrupting the row title to 'Alpaca Server Addr3ss' failed both cases, i.e. the tests depend on the row existing and on its write-through.
fixes.caveats: The verifier's grep was run against a tree that predates the row; connection_settings.dart was rewritten after the findings file was aggregated.

fixes.title: One failed 'Connect to Server' attempt drops the app out of Local mode permanently
fixes.summary: Closed exactly where the verifier said the decision lives, and closed twice. (1) The connect dialog records whether it is displacing a local FfiBackend (connection_settings.dart:559-561 `hadLocalBackend` = neither NetworkBackend nor DisconnectedBackend) and, on a failed handshake, calls _restoreLocalBackend() -> backendProvider.notifier.useLocalBackend() (:586-587, :603-616) before reporting 'Connection failed: <e>\nStill working locally on this computer.'; a restore that itself fails is named rather than hidden. The dialog stays open so the operator can correct the address. (2) connection_settings.dart:143-158 adds a 'Work Locally' row whenever the backend is disconnected on a desktop platform — the missing UI caller for useLocalBackend() that made relaunching the only way back. The red shell banner (app_shell.dart:830, still keyed on `sequencerBackendProvider is DisconnectedBackend`) is deliberately unchanged: it simply no longer fires, because a failed OPTIONAL connect no longer installs a DisconnectedBackend. That is the right shape — the banner was never the bug.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/connection_settings_local_fallback_test.dart -> 'a failed connect leaves the machine in local mode', 'a disconnected desktop is offered a way back to local mode'. Re-run green this wave.
fixes.revert_check: Not re-reverted this wave. Wave 5 recorded: replacing `final restoreError = hadLocalBackend ? await _restoreLocalBackend() : null;` with a constant null made 'a failed connect leaves the machine in local mode' fail (useLocalBackend called 0 times, expected 1).
fixes.caveats: backend_provider.dart:_rollbackFailedConnect still installs a fresh DisconnectedBackend; the restore happens one level up in the caller that knows what it displaced. That is the correct layer — the notifier does not know whether a local backend is appropriate for the platform — but a mobile client that fails to connect still gets the banner, which is right for a device with no rig of its own.
